\section[khud ro line]{My own line — the first writing with no model}

\label{lesson:MW-W02-mharo-khud-ro-line}



\begin{quote}
You have read signs and notices. Now write one.

Everything you have written so far had something to reach for. This does not.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — controlled composition}
Write \textbf{one line} about yourself, choosing the words yourself from a supply that is closed: only what this book has taught you.

One thing to decide deliberately before you start. The letters hang from a line drawn across the top, and that line belongs to the \textbf{word}, not to each letter. Draw the bodies first and the top line last, running it across the whole word.

Write the line. Then read it back and check that top line \textbf{before} you check anything else — one long stroke, not a row of short ones.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Does the top line belong to a letter or to a word? (\textbf{To the word.})

And what did you have to choose here that the earlier lessons chose for you? (\textbf{The words.})
\end{tcolorbox}
